lessons.title: Patterns
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • In this pattern the colour stays the same but the shape changes again and again.
  • In this pattern the shape stays the same but the colour changes again and again.
  • In this pattern both the shape and the colour change again and again.
  • In this pattern the shape and colour stay the same but the size changes again and again.
  • The sizes repeat in the order big, medium, small, and all the triangles are orange.
  • The shapes repeat in the order circle, square, triangle.

Patterns (book p. 121)

  • Q: Pattern 1 (book p. 121) shows: orange triangle, orange square, orange triangle, orange square, orange triangle, orange square. What is this pattern made up of?
    Ans: Rule: In this pattern the colour stays the same but the shape changes again and again.<br/>Answer: This pattern is made up of different shapes
  • Q: Pattern 2 (book p. 121) shows: purple square, orange square, purple square, orange square, purple square, orange square. What is this pattern made up of?
    Ans: Rule: In this pattern the shape stays the same but the colour changes again and again.<br/>Answer: This pattern is made up of different colours
  • Q: Pattern 3 (book p. 121) shows: black rectangle, pink triangle, black rectangle, pink triangle, black rectangle, pink triangle. What is this pattern made up of?
    Ans: Rule: In this pattern both the shape and the colour change again and again.<br/>Answer: This pattern is made up of different shapes and colours
  • Q: Pattern 4 (book p. 121) shows green circles in the order: big, medium, small, big, medium, small, big, medium, small. What is this pattern made up of?
    Ans: Rule: In this pattern the shape and colour stay the same but the size changes again and again.<br/>Answer: This pattern is made up of different sizes

Complete the Patterns (book p. 122)

  • Q: Colour the shapes to complete the pattern (book p. 122, row 1): orange big triangle, orange medium triangle, orange small triangle, followed by uncoloured triangles. How does the pattern continue?
    Ans: Rule: The sizes repeat in the order big, medium, small, and all the triangles are orange.<br/>Colour the uncoloured triangles big, medium, small, then big, medium, small.<br/>Answer: Big triangle, medium triangle, small triangle, repeating, all orange
  • Q: Colour the shapes to complete the pattern (book p. 122, row 2): green circle, purple square, orange triangle, followed by uncoloured circles, squares and triangles. How does the pattern continue?
    Ans: Rule: The shapes repeat in the order circle, square, triangle.<br/>Colour each circle green, each square purple and each triangle orange.<br/>Answer: Circle, square, triangle, repeating
  • Q: Colour the shapes to complete the pattern (book p. 122, row 3): black rectangle, orange rectangle, black rectangle, orange rectangle, black rectangle, orange rectangle, followed by uncoloured rectangles. How does the pattern continue?
    Ans: Rule: The colours repeat in the order black, orange.<br/>Colour the uncoloured rectangles black, orange, black, orange, black, orange.<br/>Answer: Black rectangle, orange rectangle, repeating
  • Q: Complete the pattern (book p. 122): big purple square, small purple square, big purple square, small purple square, big purple square, small purple square, ____, ____
    Ans: Rule: The sizes repeat in the order big square, small square.<br/>After a small square comes a big square, then a small square.<br/>Answer: Big square, small square
  • Q: Complete the pattern (book p. 122): green circle, orange triangle, pink circle, green circle, orange triangle, pink circle, ____, ____
    Ans: Rule: The pattern repeats in the order green circle, orange triangle, pink circle.<br/>After two full rounds, the pattern starts again.<br/>Answer: Green circle, orange triangle
  • Q: Complete the pattern (book p. 122): red triangle, red circle, red triangle, red circle, red triangle, red circle, ____, ____
    Ans: Rule: The shapes repeat in the order triangle, circle.<br/>After a circle comes a triangle, then a circle.<br/>Answer: Triangle, circle

Tick the Correct Answer to Complete Each Pattern (book p. 123)

    Ans: Small triangle, big triangle

lessons.title: Position — Inside, Outside, Above and Below
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • A person sitting within something is inside it.
  • A person standing out of something is outside it.
  • Outside means not within something.
  • Inside means within something.
  • Outside means not within the home.
  • Above means higher than something.

Inside or Outside (book p. 125)

  • Q: Look at the tent picture on book p. 125. Where is Samra?
    Ans: Rule: A person sitting within something is inside it.<br/>Samra is sitting within the tent.<br/>Answer: Samra is inside the tent
  • Q: Look at the tent picture on book p. 125. Where is Saad?
    Ans: Rule: A person standing out of something is outside it.<br/>Saad is standing out of the tent, on the grass.<br/>Answer: Saad is outside the tent

  • Q: Tick the picture where the cat is outside the box (book p. 126). In the left picture the cat is sitting inside the box. In the right picture the cat is sitting beside the box. Which picture do you tick?
    Ans: Rule: Outside means not within something.<br/>The cat beside the box is not within the box.<br/>Answer: Tick the right picture, where the cat is sitting beside (outside) the box
  • Q: Colour the picture where the biscuits are inside the jar (book p. 126). The left jar has biscuits in it. The right jar is empty and the biscuit is lying outside it. Which picture do you colour?
    Ans: Rule: Inside means within something.<br/>The biscuits in the left jar are within the jar.<br/>Answer: Colour the left picture, the jar with the biscuits inside it
  • Q: Encircle the hen and chicks which are outside their home (book p. 126).
    Ans: Rule: Outside means not within the home.<br/>The hen and the three yellow chicks standing on the ground on the right are not within the hen house.<br/>Answer: Encircle the hen and the three chicks standing outside the hen house

Above or Below (book p. 127)

    Ans: Rule: Above means higher than something.<br/>The clock hangs higher than the framed picture.<br/>Answer: The clock is above the picture
  • Q: Look at the room picture on book p. 127. Is the sofa above or below the picture?

lessons.title: Position — Over, Under, Far, Near, Before and After
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • Over means above and across something.
  • Under means below something.
  • Over means above something.
  • Near means at a small distance from something.
  • Far means at a long distance from something.
  • Far means at a long distance.

Over or Under (book p. 129)

  • Q: Encircle the boy under the slide (book p. 130). One boy is coming down the slide and a small boy is standing under the slide.

  • Q: Tick the picture where the horse is over the fence (book p. 130). In the left picture the horse is running beside the fence. In the right picture the horse is jumping across the fence. Which picture do you tick?

  • Q: Whose car is after Arham's car (book p. 133)?

lessons.title: Review — Shapes, Patterns and Position
lessons.notes_html:
Key Points

  • An object that is longer than it is wide, with 4 sides, is a rectangle.
  • An object with 4 sides that are all the same is a square.
  • An object with 3 sides and 3 corners is a triangle.
  • A round object with 0 sides and 0 corners is a circle.
  • In a square, all 4 sides are the same. In a rectangle, only the opposite sides are the same.
  • A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners.

Review Exercise (book p. 135)

  • Q: Write the correct shape for this daily life object (book p. 135): a green mat with a patterned border.
    Ans: Rule: An object that is longer than it is wide, with 4 sides, is a rectangle.<br/>The mat has 4 sides and is longer than it is wide.<br/>Answer: Rectangle
  • Q: Write the correct shape for this daily life object (book p. 135): a ludo board.
    Ans: Rule: An object with 4 sides that are all the same is a square.<br/>All four sides of the ludo board are the same.<br/>Answer: Square
  • Q: Write the correct shape for this daily life object (book p. 135): a clothes hanger.
    Ans: Rule: An object with 3 sides and 3 corners is a triangle.<br/>The hanger has 3 sides.<br/>Answer: Triangle
  • Q: Write the correct shape for this daily life object (book p. 135): a football.
    Ans: Rule: A round object with 0 sides and 0 corners is a circle.<br/>The face of the football is round.<br/>Answer: Circle
  • Q: Try Yourself (book p. 135): What is the difference between a rectangle and a square?
    Ans: Rule: In a square, all 4 sides are the same. In a rectangle, only the opposite sides are the same.<br/>A square has 4 equal sides. A rectangle has 2 long sides and 2 short sides.<br/>Answer: All sides of a square are equal, but in a rectangle only the opposite sides are equal

Review Exercise (book p. 136)

  • Q: Write the number of sides and corners of a rectangle (book p. 136).
    Ans: Rule: A rectangle has 4 sides and 4 corners.<br/>Answer: Sides: 4, Corners: 4
  • Q: Write the number of sides and corners of a square (book p. 136).
    Ans: Rule: A square has 4 sides and 4 corners.<br/>Answer: Sides: 4, Corners: 4
  • Q: Write the number of sides and corners of a circle (book p. 136).
    Ans: Rule: A circle is round, so it has 0 sides and 0 corners.<br/>Answer: Sides: 0, Corners: 0
  • Q: Write the number of sides and corners of a triangle (book p. 136).
    Ans: Rule: A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners.<br/>Answer: Sides: 3, Corners: 3
  • Q: Match the objects having the same shape (book p. 136): a slice of pizza (a triangle shape). Which object on the right has the same shape — a tyre, a TV, a square grid window, or a slice of cake?
    Ans: Rule: A pizza slice has 3 sides, so it is a triangle. Match it with the other triangle.<br/>The slice of cake also has 3 sides.<br/>Answer: The pizza slice matches the slice of cake (triangle)
  • Q: Match the objects having the same shape (book p. 136): a whole round pizza. Which object on the right has the same shape — a tyre, a TV, a square grid window, or a slice of cake?
    Ans: Rule: A whole pizza is round, so it is a circle. Match it with the other circle.<br/>The tyre is also round.<br/>Answer: The whole pizza matches the tyre (circle)
  • Q: Match the objects having the same shape (book p. 136): a square wall clock. Which object on the right has the same shape — a tyre, a TV, a square grid window, or a slice of cake?
    Ans: Rule: The wall clock has 4 equal sides, so it is a square. Match it with the other square.<br/>The grid window also has 4 equal sides.<br/>Answer: The square wall clock matches the square grid window (square)
  • Q: Match the objects having the same shape (book p. 136): a mobile phone. Which object on the right has the same shape — a tyre, a TV, a square grid window, or a slice of cake?
    Ans: Rule: A mobile phone is longer than it is wide, so it is a rectangle. Match it with the other rectangle.<br/>The TV screen is also a rectangle.<br/>Answer: The mobile phone matches the TV (rectangle)

Review Exercise (book p. 137)

  • Q: Match the object with the similar shape (book p. 137): an envelope. Is it similar to the circle, the triangle, the rectangle or the square drawn on the right?
    Ans: Rule: An envelope is longer than it is wide, with 4 sides.<br/>Answer: The envelope matches the rectangle
  • Q: Match the object with the similar shape (book p. 137): a photo frame. Is it similar to the circle, the triangle, the rectangle or the square drawn on the right?
    Ans: Rule: The photo frame has 4 sides that are all the same.<br/>Answer: The photo frame matches the square
  • Q: Match the object with the similar shape (book p. 137): a slice of pizza. Is it similar to the circle, the triangle, the rectangle or the square drawn on the right?
    Ans: Rule: A slice of pizza has 3 sides.<br/>Answer: The slice of pizza matches the triangle
  • Q: Match the object with the similar shape (book p. 137): a button. Is it similar to the circle, the triangle, the rectangle or the square drawn on the right?
    Ans: Rule: A button is round, with 0 sides and 0 corners.<br/>Answer: The button matches the circle

Review Exercise (book p. 138)

  • Q: Draw and colour the shapes to complete the pattern (book p. 138, row 1): orange circle, pink circle, light blue square, orange square, orange circle, ____, ____, ____, ____
    Ans: Rule: The pattern repeats after every 4 shapes: orange circle, pink circle, light blue square, orange square.<br/>The fifth shape, the orange circle, starts the pattern again.<br/>Answer: Pink circle, light blue square, orange square, orange circle
  • Q: Draw and colour the shapes to complete the pattern (book p. 138, row 2): blue triangle, pink rectangle, green circle, blue triangle, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____
    Ans: Rule: The pattern repeats after every 3 shapes: blue triangle, pink rectangle, green circle.<br/>The fourth shape, the blue triangle, starts the pattern again.<br/>Answer: Pink rectangle, green circle, blue triangle, pink rectangle, green circle
  • Q: Draw and colour the shapes to complete the pattern (book p. 138, row 3): purple triangle, green square, light blue circle, purple triangle, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____
    Ans: Rule: The pattern repeats after every 3 shapes: purple triangle, green square, light blue circle.<br/>The fourth shape, the purple triangle, starts the pattern again.<br/>Answer: Green square, light blue circle, purple triangle, green square, light blue circle
  • Q: Draw and colour the shapes to complete the pattern (book p. 138, row 4): red circle, green rectangle, red circle, green rectangle, ____, ____, ____, ____, ____
    Ans: Rule: The pattern repeats after every 2 shapes: red circle, green rectangle.<br/>After a green rectangle comes a red circle.<br/>Answer: Red circle, green rectangle, red circle, green rectangle, red circle
  • Q: Look at the picture and tick the correct answer (book p. 138): Ahmed is looking out from inside a play tunnel and Zara is standing outside it. Where is Ahmed?
    Options: outside, inside
    Ans: inside
  • Q: Look at the picture and tick the correct answer (book p. 138): Where is Zara?
    Options: outside, inside
    Ans: outside
  • Q: Colour the object that is under the car (book p. 138). A bird is flying over the car and a ball is lying under the car, between its wheels.
    Ans: Rule: Under means below something.<br/>The ball is below the car.<br/>Answer: Colour the ball under the car

Review Exercise (book p. 139)

  • Q: Encircle the object over the lamp (book p. 139). A bird is sitting on top of the lamp and a cat is standing on the ground beside the lamp post.
    Ans: Rule: Over means above something.<br/>The bird is sitting above the lamp.<br/>Answer: Encircle the bird on top of the lamp
  • Q: Colour the animal which is near the tree (book p. 139). A goat is standing close to the tree and a fox is standing far away on the hill.
    Ans: Rule: Near means at a small distance from something.<br/>The goat is standing close to the tree.<br/>Answer: Colour the goat near the tree
  • Q: Some kids are queuing up to get tickets (book p. 139). The queue in order is: Ahmer, Umar, Amna, Fahad. Who is standing just after Amna?
    Ans: Rule: The person behind another person in a queue is just after that person.<br/>Fahad is standing behind Amna.<br/>Answer: Fahad
  • Q: Who is standing just before Umar? (book p. 139, ticket queue: Ahmer, Umar, Amna, Fahad)
    Ans: Rule: The person in front of another person in a queue is just before that person.<br/>Ahmer is standing in front of Umar.<br/>Answer: Ahmer
  • Q: Who is standing just after Ahmer? (book p. 139, ticket queue: Ahmer, Umar, Amna, Fahad)
    Ans: Rule: The person behind another person in a queue is just after that person.<br/>Umar is standing behind Ahmer.<br/>Answer: Umar

lessons.title: Practice Activities
lessons.notes_html:
Practice Activities

  • Note (book p. 114): Unit opener picture: tell what shapes Arham sees while crossing the road — oral discussion only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 115): Help Amna find the 2-D shapes in her room in the picture — oral observation only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 116): Read the rhyme of the 2-D shapes (circle, square, rectangle, triangle) aloud — reading practice only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 117): Complete the train picture by joining the dots and colour all the rectangles — drawing and colouring practice only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 118): Help the tortoise reach the pond by colouring the squares in the grid — colouring practice only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 119): Colour all the circles in the curtain picture — colouring practice only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 120): Find the triangles in the bear picture and colour them green — colouring practice only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 123): Colour the mangoes and the suns to create patterns of your own choice — free colouring practice only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 124): Position unit opener picture: say who is outside the room — oral discussion only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 125): Try Yourself: tell what is inside your own bag — oral, personal answer only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 131): Try Yourself: tell whether the school is far from your home or the mosque — oral, personal answer only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 132): Draw a cat far from the pond and colour it — drawing and colouring practice only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 133): Try Yourself: tell who is sitting before you in the classroom — oral, personal answer only, no written answer.
  • Note (book p. 136): Draw each shape (rectangle, square, circle, triangle) in the table — drawing practice only, no written answer; the numbers of sides and corners are solved in the Review Exercise above.
  • Note (book p. 137): Colour the circles blue, the squares green, the rectangles yellow and the triangles red in the dotted picture — colouring practice only, no written answer.
